summary: Albania’s NDC pairs restoration with forest conservation and agricultural measures. Restoration is centred on new afforestation at 300 ha per year—about 0.03% of current forest area annually—while a mixed restoration-conservation forest-management action is applied progressively to 5,000 ha per year, about 0.43% of the 11,508 km² forest area annually. Conservation measures target a 5% reduction in wildfire risk, a 4% decrease in fuelwood consumption between 2016 and 2030, and a 3% reduction in fuelwood-harvesting losses. Agricultural actions include 100 ha of agroforestry and improved soil practices covering 20% of cultivated cropland by 2030, plus restoration of irrigation on 360,000 ha of potentially irrigable arable land, equivalent to about 26.6% of the mapped agricultural area. The mixed grassland action also expands sustainable management to enhance carbon sequestration and biodiversity, from 2% in 2021 to 20% by 2030, roughly 278 km² of currently mapped grassland.
